Subject: Voucher conversion — can we make it programmatic?

Jonas,

Thanks again for yesterday's demo — Lunar Ventures loved the latency profile on the dedicated instance. We have a question that came up internally around the accelerator vouchers we were offered: our engineering org wants to automate conversion of voucher credits into committed reserved capacity based on usage thresholds (monthly spend or sustained tpm).

Specifically: is there a way for us to set a programmatic trigger (API or webhook) that will convert remaining voucher balance into a discounted reserved commitment once we hit X tokens or Y sustained spend for 2 consecutive months? Our finance team would prefer this to be an automated flow rather than a manual procurement step.

If there's a security/compliance or legal limitation here, please flag it. I attached a short projection (MVP-usage-projection.xlsx) so you can see the cadence we expect.

Best,
Sara
Sara Patel
Head of Platform
Lunar Ventures

Subject: Re: Voucher conversion — can we make it programmatic?

Sara — thanks for the clear ask and for the projection. Looping in Ben (pricing) and Lauren (finance ops) so we can propose an operational path.

Short answer: yes, we can make most of this programmatic, but there are three places we need to be explicit about trade-offs:

- Audit & billing reconciliation: automated conversions create accounting events (commit start date, proration) that must align with your procurement calendar. Finance will want a clear audit trail and an optional human approval step.
- SLA/Capacity guarantees: converting vouchers to Reserved Capacity normally requires a minimum lead time for capacity allocation and an agreed commit term. For truly instantaneous programmatic conversion we can offer a short grace buffer but not instant physical GPU allocation in all regions.
- Pricing/discount tiers: we can support tiered discounts tied to the conversion trigger (e.g., 10% off for 3-month commit, 18% off for 12-month commit) but the trigger definition must be deterministic (token thresholds, average monthly spend, or sustained tpm).

Proposal (high level): implement a programmatic trigger that converts remaining voucher balance into a 3-month reserved commitment if Lunar hits either 150M tokens in a 30-day window or $25k in monthly bill for 2 consecutive months. Conversion would create an invoice with proration and start a 3-month term. We will expose the trigger via API and emit a webhook with a 72-hour review window where your admin can cancel the conversion before it finalizes.

Ben/Lauren — can you confirm if those thresholds are operationally workable and what discount band we can attach for a 3-month vs 12-month auto-conversion?

Thanks,
Jonas
Jonas Weber
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Voucher conversion — can we make it programmatic?

Jonas — thanks for the clear framing. Operational notes from pricing: we can support the API + webhook flow Jonas described. My suggested pricing bands to propose to the customer:

- Auto-convert to 3-month reserved commit: 12% discount to hosted list rates, with proration of remaining voucher balance applied to first invoice.
- Auto-convert to 12-month reserved commit: 20% discount and a small upfront credit requirement (to protect against immediate churn).
- If customer cancels within the webhook 72-hour review window, we reverse the pending action and no invoice is issued.

Two caveats: any programmatic flow that modifies commit terms must be signed off in an addendum to the MAP (mutual action plan). Legal requests an e-signature on the addendum prior to the first programmatic conversion event. I attached a draft MAP addendum (draft-MAP-v1.docx) with placeholders for thresholds and discounts.

Lauren — will finance require any additional controls (e.g., PO matching or vendor code) for automated invoice creation?

Thanks,
Ben
Ben Carter

Thanks Jonas and Ben — this is promising. Quick counterpoints from our side:

- Thresholds: Lunar would prefer a smaller initial threshold for the MVP — 75M tokens or $12k monthly for two months — because our team wants to lock in predictable capacity before a big hiring push. We can agree to the 3-month term on first conversion and a 12-month auto-upgrade if we sustain spend for 4 months.
- Review window: 72 hours is fine, but our SREs want a machine-readable payload that includes the projected 90-day burn so we can run a dry-run in staging.
- Legal/signature: we can sign an addendum but prefer a lightweight e-ack (checkbox + admin email) for the first conversion; DocuSign only for 12-month triggers.

I've attached the projection and highlighted months where we expect ramp. If you can update the MAP addendum with the 75M / $12k threshold and the staged upgrade path I'll get product and finance to review.

Best,
Sara
